source: Schroeder & Kucera (2022) Refutation text facilitates learning: a meta-analysis of between-subjects experiments
finding: Refutation text (state the misconception, refute it, give the right account) beats other texts by a moderate amount.
numbers: g=0.41, 95% CI [0.30,0.51]; 44 independent comparisons from 33 studies; n=3,869; Q(43)=109.59, I2=60.8%.
limits: Heterogeneity is substantial. Most studies were science concepts with low personal stakes.
agent_relevance: Supports a scaffold step that names the old frame, shows why it fails, then supplies the new one (O8 reframe) rather than just adding facts.

source: Schroeder & Kucera (2022) Refutation text facilitates learning: a meta-analysis of between-subjects experiments
finding: Publication-bias check: the funnel plot looked symmetrical, but trim-and-fill still shrinks the effect.
numbers: Egger t(42)=0.55, one-tailed p=0.29; trim-and-fill adds 10 studies on the left; adjusted g=0.28, 95% CI [0.16,0.39].
limits: Adjusted effect is small to moderate. Real effect likely nearer 0.3 than 0.4.
agent_relevance: Plan for a modest gain from explicit refutation, not a large one.

source: Schroeder & Kucera (2022) Refutation text facilitates learning: a meta-analysis of between-subjects experiments
finding: Moderators mostly did nothing: domain (science, social science, maths), images, screen versus paper, text length, and test timing all failed to moderate the effect.
numbers: Images k=9 with effect similar to text-only. One moderator test reported Qb(2)=0.63, p=0.73. Few studies tested more than a month later.
limits: Few studies outside science; lack of moderators may reflect low power.
agent_relevance: Refutation benefit is robust to format, so prompt length is not the lever. Content structure is.

source: Tippett (2010) refutation text review, as reported in Schroeder & Kucera (2022)
finding: Older review: refutation text helped in grades 3-10 (10 studies) but not in K-2 (1 study) or grade 11+ (11 studies).
numbers: 22 studies in Tippett's review. The 2022 meta-analysis asks whether this still holds a decade later.
limits: Secondhand report of Tippett; read only through the 2022 paper.
agent_relevance: Age pattern hints that strong prior frames resist a text-only refutation. Do not assume a refutation always works on a deeply entrenched frame.

source: Xie et al. (2024) Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: LLM behavior in knowledge conflicts
finding: LLMs accept a single coherent counter-evidence passage readily, but cling to their stored answer when evidence mixes supportive and conflicting items.
numbers: ChatGPT picks the memory answer 3.7% of the time when no evidence supports it and 99.8% when all evidence does (table, PopQA). GPT-4: 8.9% vs 99.8%.
limits: Counter-memory was generated by ChatGPT; PopQA and StrategyQA; models of 2023.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue of Kuhnian resistance: given any consistent evidence for the old frame, the model keeps it. A reframe trigger must not hand the model confirming snippets.
quote: LLMs can be highly receptive to external evidence even when that conflicts with their parametric memory

source: Xie et al. (2024) Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth
finding: The more popular the fact, the stronger the stickiness: confirmation bias grows with how often the model saw the entity.
numbers: GPT-4 shows an 80% memorization ratio on the most popular questions when memory and counter-evidence are both shown. Evidence order shifts results by more than 5 points, over 30 points for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B.
limits: Fluctuation depends on model; ordering effects are large for weaker models.
agent_relevance: Entrenched frames are the hardest to leave. Randomise order of old-versus-new evidence and test both orders.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Self-correction helps only when an oracle label tells the model it was wrong. Without that signal it lowers accuracy.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 standard, 38.1 after one self-correction round, 41.8 after two. With oracle labels GSM8K 75.9 -> 95.5 (GPT-3.5) and 84.3 -> 97.5 (GPT-4).
limits: Oracle comparisons are not true self-correction. GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA only.
agent_relevance: Matches G1 and G2: doubt only on a real signal (a failed check) and revise from actual output, never from the model's feeling that it may be wrong.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Why self-revision fails: the model cannot judge its own reasoning, so it flips right answers to wrong ones more often than wrong to right.
numbers: GSM8K: GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time after two rounds. GPT-4 on GSM8K: 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0 over rounds. A prompt saying the answer could be right or wrong did not remove the drop.
limits: Feedback-prompt variants were tested on GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2.
agent_relevance: An impasse detector must be code (failed check, disagreement), not an 'are you sure?' prompt.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks
finding: When a task's default assumptions change (base-9 arithmetic, 1-based indexing, rotated board), models stay above chance but fall consistently below their default-task level.
numbers: 11 task pairs; GPT-4 0-shot CoT; 1,000 two-digit sums per base for bases 8, 9, 10, 11, 16. GPT-3.5 parseable Python outputs fall from 99% (default) to 62%, 71% and 75% for flipped and rotated drawing settings.
limits: Counterfactual worlds can be harder in themselves; the authors check difficulty but cannot fully separate the effects.
agent_relevance: Models lean on narrow memorised procedures. A reframe that changes the base assumption must be checked by an independent test, not trusted.
quote: performance substantially and consistently degrades compared to the default conditions

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting?
finding: Memorisation signature: in base-10 addition accuracy falls slowly as digits grow; in other bases it falls fast. Zero-shot chain of thought also hurt some default cases.
numbers: 2-, 3- and 4-digit addition on GPT-4. 0-shot CoT hurt PaLM-2 base-10 and base-16 addition and GPT chord-playing in the default tuning.
limits: Memorisation is the authors' inference.
agent_relevance: If a problem looks like a famous one, expect pattern-matching to the usual answer. A twist is an impasse signal worth a code-level check.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search: inductive reasoning with language models
finding: Proposing several abstract hypotheses, coding each as a program and running it on examples beats direct prompting on ARC.
numbers: ARC random 100-task subset: 30% with LLM-summarised hypotheses vs 17% direct prompting; 33% when a human chose among LLM hypotheses.
limits: GPT-4; a 100-task subset; programs verified only on the given examples (G3: fitting examples is not proof).
agent_relevance: Closest working model of a computed 'new frame' step: generate candidate frames, then test by execution.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld: virtual environment for automated scientific discovery agents
finding: Strong LLM agents do poorly at full discovery cycles that need forming and revising hypotheses; humans do far better.
numbers: Best procedure agent (ReAct) completed 38% of Easy and 18% of Challenge tasks. Best explanatory agent (Hypothesizer) found 34% of gold knowledge on Easy and 8% on Challenge. Humans: 66% completion and 55% knowledge (up to 11 scientists, 16 tasks). 120 tasks over 8 topics.
limits: Simulated environment; agent models of mid-2024; human subset smaller.
agent_relevance: Agents handle components (measuring) but not end-to-end revision of explanation. This is the gap an impasse/reframe operator should address.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld
finding: On isolated unit-test tasks agents score moderately, so the failure is in chaining and revising, not in basic tool use.
numbers: Unit-test tasks: completion rates in the 60%+ range (Table 5).
limits: Averages hide wide variation across tasks.
agent_relevance: Test the operator on whole-loop tasks, not single steps.

source: Zengilowski et al. (2021) refutation text review, as reported in Schroeder & Kucera (2022)
finding: Zengilowski et al. observed that refutation text studies cover a narrow range of topics, mostly low-belief science concepts.
numbers: No counts read.
limits: Second-hand through the 2022 meta-analysis.
agent_relevance: Evidence for reframing may not transfer to identity-laden or high-stakes frames.

source: Posner, Strike, Hewson & Gertzog (1982) Accommodation of a scientific conception
finding: Classic model: change needs dissatisfaction with the old conception, plus a new one that is intelligible, plausible and fruitful.
numbers: Four conditions; theory paper, no sample.
limits: Not opened. Later work criticised it for ignoring motivation and context.
agent_relevance: Gives four code-checkable gates for the reframe step: old frame failing, new frame understandable, plausible, and productive.

source: Kendeou et al., Knowledge Revision Components (KReC), as described in Schroeder & Kucera (2022)
finding: New and old information both activate; revision occurs when the new wins the competition for activation.
numbers: Theory; no single number.
limits: Rival to replacement views: old knowledge stays and competes.
agent_relevance: Keep the old frame visible and make it lose a test, instead of deleting it.

source: Outdated-information activation and illustrations (2026), two online experiments
finding: Pictures with the updated fact did not stop the old fact from being activated while reading.
numbers: Experiment 1 N=322; Experiment 2 N=357 (with causal explanations). Responses to old-fact statements were faster after the target sentence than before it in both, with or without illustrations.
limits: Reading-time task; short texts; null result for illustration.
agent_relevance: Even after correction, the old frame is still active. Do not expect one correction to erase it; keep the check running.

source: Outdated-information activation and illustrations (2026)
finding: Background cited in the paper: outdated information is automatically activated after updating (Johnson & Seifert 1994; O'Brien et al.).
numbers: A causal explanation of the update did not remove the effect in Experiment 2.
limits: Background citations, not reread.
agent_relevance: Supports the coexistence view over a clean overwrite.

source: Conceptual prevalence study of falling bodies (2023), 953 participants
finding: Misconceptions coexist with correct rules. Physics training does not always remove them, and some get stronger.
numbers: N=953 across schooling and teaching levels. Adherence to the correct mass-and-drag rule decreased with experience (r=-.267, p<.001; F(9,940)=10.74). Secondary and college teachers scored lowest, near the 33% chance level of a three-choice question.
limits: Online reaction-time task; unequal group sizes; extreme groups small (preschool/primary n=19).
agent_relevance: Trained experts can be worse in a context that cues the wrong rule. A frame can be right in one setting and wrong in another; check the context first.

source: Conceptual prevalence study of falling bodies (2023)
finding: Most conceptual gains happen before secondary school; improvement slows once physics training starts.
numbers: Authors call this paradoxical; university professors escape the trend.
limits: Cross-sectional, not longitudinal.
agent_relevance: Instruction alone is a weak lever. Gains need a trigger and a test, not exposure.

source: Primary vs secondary evidence and 5-year-olds' balance theories (2020)
finding: A short exposure to anomalous evidence moved children's balance theories, and a hands-on activity worked as well as a picture book.
numbers: N=102 children, 34 per condition. Mass theorists rose from 13% (13/102) at pretest to 27% (27/102) at post-test. Control with unrelated book: 3/34 mass theorists post-test, versus 12/34 in each evidence condition.
limits: Age 5 only; short-term; coder agreement kappa=0.82.
agent_relevance: Anomalous evidence plus explanation changes theory, and source type matters little. An agent can use a supplied anomaly, not only one it finds itself.

source: Primary vs secondary evidence and balance theories (2020)
finding: Many children sat in an intermediate state with two inconsistent theories, so change passes through a mixed state.
numbers: 'Transition Theorists' were 34% (35/102) at pretest and 50% (51/102) at post-test.
limits: Same sample; four theorist categories.
agent_relevance: Expect a mixed state between old and new frames; do not score the transition as failure.

source: Extended refutation text and humor on p-value misconceptions (2026)
finding: A 10-minute extended refutation text sharply cut p-value misconceptions in psychology students.
numbers: N=157, 2x2 design; intervention vs control on conceptual change score t(153)=7.32, d=2.34; 98.1% made at least one error at pretest.
limits: Immediate post-test, subjective-certainty scoring, no long-term follow-up; effect far above the 0.41 meta-analytic mean.
agent_relevance: Large gains happen when the correction targets a precise, well-known error. Specific named errors are good reframe targets.

source: Student sensemaking with anomalous data (2024), think-aloud study
finding: What students decide to do with an anomaly (keep, remove, recollect, mitigate) depends on the cause they explain it with.
numbers: Six students, about 16 hours of think-aloud interviews in an introductory physics lab.
limits: Qualitative; six students; technical anomalies only.
agent_relevance: The explanation of cause is the fork point: error in procedure versus error in theory. The agent should make this fork explicit and test each branch with code.

source: Plausibility transition model for sensemaking (2023)
finding: Explanation building is triggered by surprises and anomalies, and plausibility judgments gate each step of the story.
numbers: Built from 23 convenience-sample cases (for example Air France 447).
limits: Exploratory, post-hoc cases, no effect size.
agent_relevance: Fits the impasse trigger: a surprise opens a search for a new story; a plausibility check gates each move.

source: Dunbar (1997) How scientists think: on-line creativity and conceptual change in science
finding: In-vivo study of molecular biology labs: unexpected results were common, and groups usually first blamed method, later changed the model.
numbers: Exact counts not read here.
limits: Not opened; recalled at abstract level.
agent_relevance: Method-versus-theory fork is a long-observed pattern; code should force a replicate before declaring a theory failure.

source: Chinn & Brewer (1993) The role of anomalous data in knowledge acquisition
finding: Taxonomy of seven responses to anomalous data: ignore, reject, exclude, hold in abeyance, reinterpret, peripheral change, theory change.
numbers: Taxonomy, no effect size.
limits: Not opened. Theory change is the rarest response in their account.
agent_relevance: Default response to an anomaly is to protect the theory. The agent must be built to use the rare response on purpose.

source: Shtulman & Valcarcel (2012) Scientific knowledge suppresses but does not supplant earlier intuitions
finding: Adults verifying science statements were slower and less accurate when the true answer conflicted with the old intuition.
numbers: Reaction time and accuracy gaps; exact figures not read here.
limits: Not opened; title confirmed via Crossref only.
agent_relevance: Supports coexistence: old frames stay and are suppressed, so reframing needs repeated checks.
